frequency_question: How often does a central bank deploy an incremental cash reserve ratio instrument when facing excess liquidity conditions within a comparable time window?
membership_rule: Members are instances where a central bank officially introduced an incremental or supplemental reserve requirement on commercial bank deposits to manage systemic liquidity. Excluded are standard, permanent changes to baseline reserve requirements or ordinary open market operations.

cases.name: PBoC incremental reserve requirement adjustments (various historical tightening phases)

provenance_note: 2 cases named, 4 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.0x)
coverage_note: 2 named instances; estimated approximately 4 comparable major policy cycles globally in the past two decades.
known_gaps: Limited strictly to major emerging market central bank discretionary liquidity tools.
skeleton: Central bank policy cycles involving surplus liquidity management across major emerging market central banks prone to capital inflows over four distinct liquidity-surge epochs.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 4 identified major liquidity-surge episodes where targeted incremental reserve tools were considered and deployed by central bank principals.
validity_reason: Central bank mandates and structural approaches to liquidity management evolve slowly over decades.
